1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""check-dod.py
3	
4	Definition-of-Done checker for a single geeky-implement task. Embodies "verify,
5	don't trust": instead of believing the agent that a task is finished, assert the
6	durable signals on disk before the task may move to Done.
7	
8	Checks for task <ID> in <folder> (missing => ERROR unless noted):
9	  - a per-task notes file tasks/<ID>-*.notes.md exists
10	  - <ID> is placed in the Done lane of kanban.md
11	  - handoff.md mentions <ID>
12	  - WARNING if <ID> still appears in a non-Done lane (In Progress / Blocked / ...)
13	
14	It also extracts and prints the task's "Tests/Validation Before Next Task" block
15	so the orchestrator can re-run those commands itself (this script does not execute
16	them — running is the caller's job, kept framework- and shell-agnostic).
17	
18	Contract: argv in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, human summary on stdout.
19	  --json emits a machine-readable object.
20	
21	Usage:
22	  python check-dod.py --path "/abs/docs/feature" --task T3
23	  python check-dod.py "/abs/docs/feature" T3 --json
24	"""
25	
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import argparse
29	import json
30	import re
31	import sys
32	from pathlib import Path
33	
34	KNOWN_LANES = ("Backlog", "Ready", "In Progress", "In Review", "Blocked", "Done")
35	HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^\s{0,3}#{1,6}\s+(.*\S)\s*$")
36	
37	
38	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
39	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True)
40	    p.add_argument("--path", dest="path")
41	    p.add_argument("--task", dest="task")
42	    p.add_argument("pos_path", nargs="?", default=None)
43	    p.add_argument("pos_task", nargs="?", default=None)
44	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="as_json", action="store_true")
45	    return p.parse_args()
46	
47	
48	def lane_for_heading(heading: str) -> str | None:
49	    norm = heading.strip().lower()
50	    if "validation" in norm:
51	        return None
52	    for lane in KNOWN_LANES:
53	        if norm == lane.lower() or norm.startswith(lane.lower()):
54	            return lane
55	    return None
56	
57	
58	def lanes_for_task(kanban_text: str, task_id: str) -> list[str]:
59	    found: list[str] = []
60	    current: str | None = None
61	    tid_re = re.compile(rf"\b{re.escape(task_id)}\b", re.IGNORECASE)
62	    for line in kanban_text.splitlines():
63	        hm = HEADING_RE.match(line)
64	        if hm:
65	            current = lane_for_heading(hm.group(1))
66	            continue
67	        if current and tid_re.search(line) and current not in found:
68	            found.append(current)
69	    return found
70	
71	
72	def extract_validation_block(task_text: str) -> str:
73	    lines = task_text.splitlines()
74	    start = None
75	    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
76	        if re.search(r"Tests\s*/\s*Validation", line, re.IGNORECASE):
77	            start = i + 1
78	            break
79	    if start is None:
80	        return ""
81	    out: list[str] = []
82	    for line in lines[start:]:
83	        # Stop at the next section label (Estimate:/Priority:/heading).
84	        if re.match(r"^\s*[#*\s]*(Estimate|Priority)\b", line, re.IGNORECASE):
85	            break
86	        if re.match(r"^\s{0,3}#{1,6}\s+\S", line):
87	            break
88	        out.append(line)
89	    return "\n".join(out).strip()
90	
91	
92	def main() -> int:
93	    args = parse_args()
94	    path_str = args.path or args.pos_path
95	    task_id = (args.task or args.pos_task or "").upper()
96	    if not path_str or not task_id:
97	        print("USAGE: check-dod.py --path <folder> --task <ID> [--json]")
98	        return 1
99	
100	    folder = Path(path_str)
101	    if not folder.is_dir():
102	        msg = f"MISSING_FOLDER: {folder}"
103	        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
104	        return 1
105	
106	    errors: list[str] = []
107	    warnings: list[str] = []
108	
109	    # 1. notes file
110	    tasks_dir = folder / "tasks"
111	    notes = []
112	    if tasks_dir.is_dir():
113	        notes = [f.name for f in tasks_dir.iterdir()
114	                 if f.is_file() and re.match(rf"^{re.escape(task_id)}\b", f.name, re.IGNORECASE)
115	                 and f.name.lower().endswith(".notes.md")]
116	    if not notes:
117	        errors.append(f"no per-task notes file tasks/{task_id}-*.notes.md")
118	
119	    # 2/4. kanban placement
120	    kanban = folder / "kanban.md"
121	    lanes: list[str] = []
122	    if not kanban.is_file():
123	        errors.append("kanban.md not found")
124	    else:
125	        lanes = lanes_for_task(kanban.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), task_id)
126	        if "Done" not in lanes:
127	            errors.append(f"{task_id} is not in the Done lane (found in: {', '.join(lanes) or 'no lane'})")
128	        non_done = [l for l in lanes if l != "Done"]
129	        if non_done:
130	            warnings.append(f"{task_id} also appears in: {', '.join(non_done)}")
131	
132	    # 3. handoff mention
133	    handoff = folder / "handoff.md"
134	    if not handoff.is_file():
135	        warnings.append("handoff.md not found")
136	    elif not re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(task_id)}\b", handoff.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), re.IGNORECASE):
137	        warnings.append(f"handoff.md does not mention {task_id}")
138	
139	    # validation block (informational)
140	    validation = ""
141	    if tasks_dir.is_dir():
142	        for f in tasks_dir.iterdir():
143	            if (f.is_file() and re.match(rf"^{re.escape(task_id)}\b", f.name, re.IGNORECASE)
144	                    and f.name.lower().endswith(".md") and not f.name.lower().endswith(".notes.md")):
145	                validation = extract_validation_block(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
146	                break
147	
148	    ok = not errors
149	    summary = f"{'DOD_OK' if ok else 'DOD_INCOMPLETE'}: {task_id}"
150	
151	    if args.as_json:
152	        print(json.dumps({
153	            "ok": ok, "task": task_id, "errors": errors, "warnings": warnings,
154	            "lanes": lanes, "validation_block": validation,
155	        }, indent=2))
156	    else:
157	        print(summary)
158	        for e in errors:
159	            print(f"  ERROR:   {e}")
160	        for w in warnings:
161	            print(f"  WARNING: {w}")
162	        if validation:
163	            print("  Re-run this task's validation block (verify, don't trust):")
164	            for line in validation.splitlines():
165	                print(f"    | {line}")
166	
167	    return 0 if ok else 1
168	
169	
170	if __name__ == "__main__":
171	    sys.exit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""validate-kanban.py
3	
4	Deterministic integrity check for a geeky-plan kanban.md against the tasks/ folder.
5	Replaces LLM self-report ("I updated the board") with a fail-stop check.
6	
7	Checks (errors fail the run; warnings do not):
8	  ERROR   - a task file in tasks/ is not placed in any lane (untracked)
9	  ERROR   - a task id appears in more than one lane (ambiguous placement)
10	  WARNING - a task id referenced in the kanban has no matching task file (dangling)
11	  WARNING - In Progress count exceeds the WIP cap (default 3)
12	  WARNING - a known lane heading is entirely missing
13	
14	Recognised lanes (case-insensitive, any heading depth): Backlog, Ready,
15	In Progress, In Review, Blocked, Done. A heading containing "validation" is
16	treated as the release-gate checklist, not a task lane.
17	
18	Contract (matches the other validators):
19	  argv in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, human summary on stdout.
20	  --json emits a machine-readable object instead of the human summary.
21	
22	Usage:
23	  python validate-kanban.py --path "/abs/path/to/docs/feature-folder"
24	  python validate-kanban.py "/abs/path/to/docs/feature-folder" --wip 3 --json
25	"""
26	
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	import argparse
30	import json
31	import re
32	import sys
33	from pathlib import Path
34	
35	# Ordered so that more specific "In ..." lanes are tested before short names.
36	KNOWN_LANES = ("Backlog", "Ready", "In Progress", "In Review", "Blocked", "Done")
37	
38	HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^\s{0,3}#{1,6}\s+(.*\S)\s*$")
39	TASK_ID_RE = re.compile(r"\bT\d+\b", re.IGNORECASE)
40	TASK_FILE_RE = re.compile(r"^T\d+", re.IGNORECASE)
41	NOTES_RE = re.compile(r"\.notes\.md$", re.IGNORECASE)
42	
43	
44	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
45	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True)
46	    p.add_argument("--path", dest="path", required=False)
47	    p.add_argument("positional", nargs="?", default=None)
48	    p.add_argument("--wip", type=int, default=3, help="In Progress WIP cap (default 3)")
49	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="as_json", action="store_true")
50	    return p.parse_args()
51	
52	
53	def lane_for_heading(heading: str) -> str | None:
54	    """Return the canonical lane name for a heading, or None."""
55	    norm = heading.strip().lower()
56	    if "validation" in norm:
57	        return None
58	    for lane in KNOWN_LANES:
59	        if norm == lane.lower() or norm.startswith(lane.lower()):
60	            return lane
61	    return None
62	
63	
64	def task_ids_from_files(tasks_dir: Path) -> set[str]:
65	    ids: set[str] = set()
66	    if not tasks_dir.is_dir():
67	        return ids
68	    for f in tasks_dir.iterdir():
69	        if not f.is_file():
70	            continue
71	        if NOTES_RE.search(f.name) or not f.name.lower().endswith(".md"):
72	            continue
73	        m = TASK_FILE_RE.match(f.name)
74	        if m:
75	            ids.add(m.group(0).upper())
76	    return ids
77	
78	
79	def parse_kanban(text: str) -> tuple[dict[str, set[str]], set[str]]:
80	    """Map canonical lane -> set of task ids referenced under it, and the set of
81	    lane headings actually present in the document."""

99	def build_report(folder: Path, wip_cap: int) -> dict:
100	    errors: list[str] = []
101	    warnings: list[str] = []
102	
103	    kanban = folder / "kanban.md"
104	    if not kanban.is_file():
105	        return {
106	            "ok": False,
107	            "errors": [f"MISSING: {kanban}"],
108	            "warnings": [],

111	        }

114	    placements, present_lanes = parse_kanban(
115	        kanban.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
116	    )
117	
118	    # Where does each id live?
119	    id_lanes: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
120	    for lane, ids in placements.items():
121	        for tid in ids:
122	            id_lanes.setdefault(tid, []).append(lane)
123	
124	    # Untracked: a real task file not placed anywhere.
125	    for tid in sorted(file_ids):
126	        if tid not in id_lanes:
127	            errors.append(f"{tid} has a task file but is not placed in any kanban lane")
128	
129	    # Ambiguous: placed in more than one lane.
130	    for tid, lanes in sorted(id_lanes.items()):
131	        if len(lanes) > 1:
132	            errors.append(f"{tid} appears in multiple lanes: {', '.join(sorted(lanes))}")
133	
134	    # Dangling: referenced in kanban but no task file.
135	    for tid in sorted(id_lanes):
136	        if file_ids and tid not in file_ids:
137	            warnings.append(f"{tid} is referenced in the kanban but has no tasks/{tid}-*.md file")
138	
139	    # Missing lanes.

141	        if lane not in present_lanes:

143

148

157	    )

**READY TO ADVANCE.** I found no blockers. I read the code and checked it against `contract.md`. I had no execution tool, so I did not run anything myself. The green 36-test run is the orchestrator's report.

**Shared contracts that Phase 2 relies on**
- **`errors.py`:** `EXIT_TX=3` and `EXIT_RULES=4` match the contract table. `LedgerError(message, exit_code)` exposes `.message` and `.exit_code`.
  - There is no constant for the usage-error code 2 or the catch-all code 1. T8 can define those itself, so this is not a blocker.
- **`read_table(path, required, exit_code)`:** It returns `(index, rows)`. `index` maps the stripped, lowercased header name to its column position. `rows` is a list of `(line_num, fields)` tuples.
  - Blank rows are skipped.
  - `line_num` is taken after the record is read, so it is correct for multiline quoted fields.
  - The field-count check uses the full header length, and extra columns are kept.
  - The header checks run in the contract order: no header, then duplicate column (the second occurrence, first duplicate in header order), then missing column (first absent name in `required` order).
  - The messages match the error table exactly: `cannot read file`, `not valid UTF-8`, `missing header`, `duplicate column '…'`, `missing column '…'`, `expected N fields, got M`, and `malformed CSV` for `csv.Error`.
  - `path` is passed through unchanged, so a relative argv path stays relative.
  - T4 and T5 must run the row checks in contract order. For transactions that is field count (done in T3), then date, then amount. For rules, T5 must put category, type, pattern, priority, regex after the field count.
- **Money API:**
  - `parse_amount` uses `fullmatch` on `-?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?` after `strip()` and returns `None` for invalid input.
  - `money_sum` adds under `MONEY_CONTEXT`, which is exact (Inexact trapped).
  - `format_money` quantizes once with ROUND_HALF_UP and prints `0.00` when the result is zero, so `-0.00` never appears.
  - `format_money` uses a separate display context that does not trap Inexact. That is correct, because the rounding is intentionally inexact.
  - The dedup key can use `Decimal` equality directly. `-4.5 == -4.50`, and `-0 == 0` with equal hashes, which O4 needs.

**Findings**

*Blockers:* none.

*Important, for Phase 2 and 3 to carry:*
- T6 must sum with `money_sum` or `MONEY_CONTEXT`, not the built-in `sum()`. Summing `Decimal`s with `sum()` uses the thread default context (28 digits) and would silently round. This is only a docstring hint today.
- T4 and T5 must prefer `parse_amount` and `read_table` rather than re-implementing them. That includes stripping the date and amount values before the regex check, and putting the stripped value in the error message.
- T8's catch-all (exit 1) should also cover `decimal.Inexact` or `InvalidOperation` raised by a pathological input. The context uses `prec=10**6`, so an amount with more than 10^6 digits would raise instead of returning an error message. This is an extreme edge case, and the contract treats exit 1 as the reserved unexpected-error code.

*Minor:*
- A file whose first line is blank gives `missing column 'date'` rather than `missing header`. The contract defines "no header" only as a 0-byte file. A BOM-only file gives `missing header`, which is a reasonable reading.
- `csvledger/cli.py` is a stub (`main` returns 0). That is expected, since T8 owns it.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""check-commit.py
3	
4	Validate a commit message against the geeky-implement format: a Conventional
5	Commits subject plus a task reference (Tasks: T<n> ...). The most natively
6	portable gate — wire it as a git commit-msg hook, a pre-commit check, or a
7	Claude PreToolUse matcher on `Bash(git commit *)`.
8	
9	Rules (violations => ERROR, exit 1):
10	  - subject matches  type(scope)!: summary  where type is one of
11	    feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|revert
12	    (scope optional; '!' optional)
13	  - subject length <= 72 chars
14	  - a task reference exists somewhere in the message: a "Tasks:" line, or a
15	    bare T<number> token (warn-only if only a bare token, error if neither).
16	
17	Message source (first that is provided):
18	  positional FILE  (git commit-msg passes the path to .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG)
19	  --message "..."
20	  stdin
21	
22	Contract: exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, human summary on stdout. --json optional.
23	
24	Usage:
25	  python check-commit.py .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG
26	  python check-commit.py --message "feat(plan): add linter\n\nTasks: T3"
27	  echo "$msg" | python check-commit.py --json
28	"""
29	
30	from __future__ import annotations
31	
32	import argparse
33	import json
34	import re
35	import sys
36	from pathlib import Path
37	
38	TYPES = "feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|revert"
39	SUBJECT_RE = re.compile(rf"^(?:{TYPES})(?:\([^)]+\))?!?: .+")
40	TASKS_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*Tasks:\s*.*\bT\d+\b", re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE)
41	BARE_TASK_RE = re.compile(r"\bT\d+\b")
42	MAX_SUBJECT = 72
43	
44	
45	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
46	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True)
47	    p.add_argument("file", nargs="?", default=None)
48	    p.add_argument("--message", dest="message", default=None)
49	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="as_json", action="store_true")
50	    return p.parse_args()
51	
52	
53	def read_message(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str | None:
54	    if args.message is not None:
55	        return args.message
56	    if args.file:
57	        p = Path(args.file)
58	        if not p.is_file():
59	            return None
60	        return p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
61	    data = sys.stdin.read()
62	    return data if data else None
63	
64	
65	def check(message: str) -> dict:
66	    # Ignore comment lines (git strips '#' lines) and blank leading lines.
67	    lines = [ln for ln in message.splitlines() if not ln.lstrip().startswith("#")]
68	    subject = next((ln for ln in lines if ln.strip()), "")
69	    body = "\n".join(lines)
70	
71	    errors: list[str] = []
72	    warnings: list[str] = []
73	
74	    if not SUBJECT_RE.match(subject):
75	        errors.append(
76	            f'subject is not Conventional Commits "type(scope): summary": {subject!r}'
77	        )
78	    if len(subject) > MAX_SUBJECT:
79	        errors.append(f"subject exceeds {MAX_SUBJECT} chars ({len(subject)})")
80	
81	    if TASKS_LINE_RE.search(body):
82	        pass
83	    elif BARE_TASK_RE.search(body):
84	        warnings.append('task referenced but no "Tasks: T<n>" line (recommended)')
85	    else:
86	        errors.append("no task reference (expected a Tasks: line with T<n>)")
87	
88	    ok = not errors
89	    return {"ok": ok, "subject": subject, "errors": errors, "warnings": warnings}
90	
91	
92	def main() -> int:
93	    args = parse_args()
94	    message = read_message(args)
95	    if message is None:
96	        msg = "NO_MESSAGE: provide a file path, --message, or pipe via stdin"
97	        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "errors": [msg]}) if args.as_json else msg)
98	        return 1
99	
100	    report = check(message)
101	    if args.as_json:
102	        print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
103	    else:
104	        print("OK: commit message valid." if report["ok"] else "INVALID_COMMIT_MESSAGE:")
105	        for e in report["errors"]:
106	            print(f"  ERROR:   {e}")
107	        for w in report["warnings"]:
108	            print(f"  WARNING: {w}")
109	    return 0 if report["ok"] else 1
110	
111	
112	if __name__ == "__main__":
113	    sys.exit(main())
114
